subject: Engineering Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer
chapters: Chapter 7: Vapor Power Cycles and Vapor Compression Refrigeration Cycles

questions.text: State and explain Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics. Explain its significance as the basis for temperature measurement. Differentiate between microscopic and macroscopic viewpoints in thermodynamics with examples.
Define Thermodynamic Property, Thermodynamic State, and Thermodynamic Equilibrium. Differentiate between Intensive and Extensive properties with examples.

A large chamber is separated into two compartments A and B maintained at different pressures. Pressure gauge A reads $180\text{ kPa}$ and pressure gauge B reads $120\text{ kPa}$. If barometric atmospheric pressure is $100\text{ kPa}$, determine the absolute pressures in compartments A and B, and find the reading of gauge C between the compartments.

Define Stored Energy vs Transient Energy. Differentiate between Heat Transfer and Work Transfer with examples. Derive expression for boundary displacement work $W = \int P dV$ for an ideal gas undergoing a Polytropic process ($P V^n = C$): $W_{1-2} = \frac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{n - 1}$. Sketch polytropic processes for $n = 0, 1, \gamma, \infty$ on a $P-V$ diagram.

A piston-cylinder device with a linear spring contains $0.05\text{ m}^3$ of gas initially at $200\text{ kPa}$. The spring ($k = 150\text{ kN/m}$) touches the piston without exerting force. Heat is supplied causing the gas to expand until volume doubles. If piston cross-sectional area is $0.25\text{ m}^2$, calculate the final pressure and total work done by the gas.

Define Pure Substance, Saturation Pressure, Saturation Temperature, Saturated Liquid, Saturated Vapor, Wet Mixture, Quality (Dryness Fraction $x$), and Critical Point. Explain the formation of saturation curve on $T-v$ and $P-v$ diagrams. Derive the expression for specific volume of a two-phase mixture: $v = v_f + x v_{fg}$.

A closed rigid container of volume $0.2\text{ m}^3$ initially contains a mixture of saturated liquid water and saturated water vapor at $100\text{ kPa}$ with quality $x = 50\%$. Heat is added until pressure reaches $200\text{ kPa}$. Sketch the process on $P-v$ and $T-v$ diagrams and determine: (a) Temperature at each state, (b) Mass of liquid and vapor at each state, and (c) Pressure if heating continues until container holds only saturated vapor.

State the First Law of Thermodynamics for a control mass undergoing a cycle ($\oint \delta Q = \oint \delta W$) and for a change of state ($Q - W = \Delta U$). State and prove that Internal Energy ($U$) is a property of the system.

Write general mass conservation and energy conservation equations for a control volume (open system) under steady state flow condition: $\dot{Q} - \dot{W} = \sum \dot{m}_e \left(h_e + \frac{V_e^2}{2} + g z_e\right) - \sum \dot{m}_i \left(h_i + \frac{V_i^2}{2} + g z_i\right)$. Reduce these equations for: (a) Adiabatic Nozzle, (b) Adiabatic Diffuser, (c) Steam Turbine, and (d) Throttle Valve.

Steam enters an adiabatic turbine at $2\text{ MPa}$ and $400^\circ\text{C}$ with velocity $200\text{ m/s}$ and leaves at $100\text{ kPa}$ as saturated vapor with velocity $80\text{ m/s}$. The mass flow rate is $1.5\text{ kg/s}$. Determine the power output developed by the turbine.

State Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the Second Law of Thermodynamics and prove their equivalence. Define Thermal Efficiency of Heat Engine ($\eta_{th} = \frac{W_{net}}{Q_H}$) and Coefficient of Performance (COP) of Refrigerator ($COP_R = \frac{Q_L}{W_{in}}$) and Heat Pump ($COP_{HP} = \frac{Q_H}{W_{in}} = COP_R + 1$).

State and prove Clausius Inequality: $\oint \frac{\delta Q}{T} \le 0$. Define Entropy ($S$). Derive $T ds$ equations ($T ds = du + P dv$ and $T ds = dh - v dP$) and derive entropy change formulas for an ideal gas undergoing constant volume and constant pressure processes.

Explain Air-Standard Otto Cycle (Constant Volume heat addition) and Diesel Cycle (Constant Pressure heat addition). Draw $P-v$ and $T-s$ diagrams. Derive expression for thermal efficiency of Otto cycle: $\eta_{th, Otto} = 1 - \frac{1}{r^{\gamma - 1}}$ and Diesel cycle: $\eta_{th, Diesel} = 1 - \frac{1}{r^{\gamma - 1}} \left[\frac{r_c^\gamma - 1}{\gamma (r_c - 1)}\right]$. Compare them for the same compression ratio and peak pressure.

Explain the Brayton Gas Turbine Cycle. Draw $P-v$ and $T-s$ diagrams and derive thermal efficiency $\eta = 1 - \frac{1}{r_p^{(\gamma-1)/\gamma}}$. An ideal Brayton cycle has a pressure ratio of 10. Air enters compressor at $300\text{ K}$ and turbine at $1200\text{ K}$. Determine its thermal efficiency and mass flow rate of air to produce $80\text{ MW}$ net power output.

questions.text: Explain Simple Ideal Rankine Cycle for steam power plants with schematic, $P-v$, and $T-s$ diagrams. Calculate turbine work, pump work, heat added in boiler, and thermal efficiency for a plant operating between boiler pressure $6\text{ MPa}$ ($400^\circ\text{C}$) and condenser pressure $10\text{ kPa}$.

Explain Modes of Heat Transfer: Fourier's Law of Conduction ($Q = -k A \frac{dT}{dx}$), Newton's Law of Cooling for Convection ($Q = h A (T_s - T_\infty)$), and Stefan-Boltzmann Law for Radiation ($Q = \epsilon \sigma A (T_s^4 - T_{surr}^4)$). Define Thermal Resistance concept for plane wall and cylinder.

An exterior wall of a house consists of a $10\text{ cm}$ layer of common brick ($k = 0.8\text{ W/mK}$) followed by a $4\text{ cm}$ layer of gypsum plaster ($k = 0.5\text{ W/mK}$). What thickness of rock wool insulation ($k = 0.055\text{ W/mK}$) should be added to reduce heat loss through the wall by $50\%$? Assume heat transfer coefficients remain unchanged.
